proofs.proof_tex:
For the mixed family, let \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), let \(\zeta\) have a centered logistic distribution independently of \(X\), draw \(A\mid X=x\) as Bernoulli with
\[
 \pi_1(x)=\frac{x^{3/2}}2,
 \qquad
 \pi_0(x)=1-\frac{x^{3/2}}2,
\]
and set \(Y(a)=a+X+\zeta\) and \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  The last equality is consistency.  Conditional construction and independence of \(\zeta\) give \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X\).  Positivity holds away from the \(P_X\)-null endpoint \(x=0\).

For \(0<t<1/2\), direct inversion gives
\[
 F_1^\pi(t)=P\{X\le(2t)^{2/3}\}=2^{2/3}t^{2/3}.
\]
Thus \(c_1=2^{2/3}\), \(\gamma_1=5/3\), and the Hall remainder is zero.  Since \(\pi_0\ge1/2\), the bounded-support convention gives \(\gamma_0=\infty\) and \(E_P(1/\pi_0)\le2\).  With \(d_1(x)=x\), \(d_0(x)=1-x\), \(\alpha_1=3/2\), and \(\alpha_0=0\),
\[
 \eta(x)=\log\frac{\pi_1(x)}{\pi_0(x)}
 =\frac32\log x+g(x),
 \qquad
 g(x)=-\log2-\log\left(1-\frac{x^{3/2}}2\right).
\]
The function \(g\) belongs to a bounded \(C^{3/2}\) ball.  This is precisely the proposed joint boundary link.  It also follows from \(\text{lem:paired-links-imply-joint-logit}\) by taking \(g_1=-\log2\) and \(g_0=\log(1-x^{3/2}/2)\).  Near \(x=0\), \(\pi_1\le1/2\), so opposite overlap holds.

Writing \(\lambda(z)=e^{-z}(1+e^{-z})^{-2}\) and \(\Lambda(z)=(1+e^{-z})^{-1}\),
\[
 f_{a\mid X}(y\mid x)=\lambda(y-a-x),
 \qquad
 m_{a,\tau}(x)=\tau-\Lambda\{q_a(\tau)-a-x\}.
\]
The bounded derivative of \(\lambda\) supplies the common conditional-density modulus, and the displayed regression is smooth.  Moreover,
\[
 f_a(\tau)=\int_0^1\lambda\{q_a(\tau)-a-x\}\,dx>0.
\]
Finiteness of \(\mathcal A\times\mathcal T\) makes the minimum positive.  Conditional on \(\pi_1(X)=t\), \(X=(2t)^{2/3}\), and therefore
\[
 |\kappa_{1,\tau}(t)-\kappa_{1,\tau}(0)|
 \le \|\lambda\|_\infty(2t)^{2/3}.
\]
Taking \(G_1\) as the law of \(1+\zeta\) verifies the tail-mark condition.  Symmetry of \(X+\zeta\) about \(1/2\) gives \(q_1(1/2)=3/2\), hence
\[
 m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{1,1/2}=\frac12-\Lambda(1/2)\ne0.
\]

For the two-heavy family choose \((\alpha_0,\alpha_1)\) in a compact rectangle contained in \((s,\infty)^2\), and put
\[
 \pi_1(x)=\frac{x^{\alpha_1}}{x^{\alpha_1}+(1-x)^{\alpha_0}},
 \qquad
 \pi_0(x)=\frac{(1-x)^{\alpha_0}}{x^{\alpha_1}+(1-x)^{\alpha_0}}.
\]
Then
\[
 \eta(x)=\alpha_1\log x-\alpha_0\log(1-x),
\]
so the joint remainder is zero.  To verify the retained Hölder condition on the paired representatives, take
\[
 g_0(x)=g_1(x)=-\log\{x^{\alpha_1}+(1-x)^{\alpha_0}\}.
\]
The compact restriction \(\alpha_a>s\) makes these functions uniformly \(C^s\).  Endpoint expansion gives
\[
 \pi_1(x)=x^{\alpha_1}\{1+O(x^\rho)\}\quad(x\downarrow0),
 \qquad
 \pi_0(x)=(1-x)^{\alpha_0}\{1+O((1-x)^\rho)\}\quad(x\uparrow1)
\]
for a common \(\rho>0\).  Monotone inversion under the uniform chart yields
\[
 F_a^\pi(t)=c_at^{1/\alpha_a}\{1+O(t^{\rho_a})\},
 \qquad
 \gamma_a=1+\alpha_a^{-1}\in(1,2).
\]
Compactness supplies the uniform constants.  The two endpoints are disjoint, giving opposite overlap, and the preceding logistic-outcome calculation gives the common mark and density moduli.  Thus the mixed and two-heavy families belong to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\), proving the proposition under the coherent joint logit representation.

At the mixed center, direct inversion of \(\pi_0(x)=1-x^{3/2}/2\) gives
\[
 F_0^\pi(t)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&t\le1/2,\\
 1-\{2(1-t)\}^{2/3},&1/2<t<1,\\
 1,&t\ge1.
 \end{cases}
\]
Consequently \(F_0^\pi(1/2+v)=4v/3+O(v^2)\), and the generalized-inverse equation \(ntF_0^\pi(t)=1\) yields
\[
 t_{0,n}=\frac12+\frac{3}{2n}+O(n^{-2}),
 \qquad h_{0,n}\to2.
\tag{F1}
\]

It remains to control the joint fit at the evaluation observations.  On this witness the Bernoulli information weight is
\[
 w(x)=\pi_0(x)\pi_1(x),
 \qquad c x^{3/2}\le w(x)\le Cx^{3/2}.
\tag{F2}
\]
Let \(V_J\) be the degree-\(r\) quasi-uniform spline space.  On the first cell, the change of variable \(u=Jx\) gives
\[
 \inf_{v\in V_J}\int_0^{1/J}x^{3/2}\{\log x-v(x)\}^2dx
 =J^{-5/2}\inf_{p\in\mathcal P_r}\int_0^1u^{3/2}\{\log u-p(u)\}^2du
 \asymp J^{-5/2}.
\tag{F3}
\]
The last infimum is positive because \(\log u\) is not a polynomial of fixed degree.  On the last cell, where \(w\) is bounded above and below, the analogous calculation gives
\[
 \inf_{v\in V_J}\int_{1-1/J}^1w(x)\{\log(1-x)-v(x)\}^2dx\asymp J^{-1}.
\tag{F4}
\]
Spline approximation of each logarithm is uniform away from its own endpoint, so near-best residuals for the two logarithms concentrate on opposite cells.  Their normalized cross inner product tends to zero by splitting the integral into the two endpoint cells and their complement and applying Cauchy--Schwarz on each piece.  On a rescaled cell, the unit sphere of the fixed finite-dimensional polynomial space is compact and its weighted squared-integral norm is continuous and strictly positive; hence its minimum is positive.  Applying this elementary compactness argument cell by cell gives the profiled information inequalities
\[
 \|r_{1,J}\|_w^2\asymp J^{-5/2},
 \qquad
 \|r_{0,J}\|_w^2\asymp J^{-1},
\tag{F5}
\]
where \(r_{1,J}\) and \(r_{0,J}\) are the residuals from profiling \(\log x\) and \(-\log(1-x)\) against the spline space and against each other.

For a joint-logit direction \(v\), direct differentiation gives score \((A-\pi_1)v\) and information \(E_P\{wv^2\}\).  On the event
\[
 \min_iX_i\ge n^{-2},
 \qquad
 \min_i(1-X_i)\ge n^{-2},
\tag{F6}
\]
all clipped log regressors at sample points are bounded by \(2\log n\); the complement has probability at most \(2/n\) by the union bound and the uniform design.  For a centered summand \(W\) with \(|W|\le b\), expansion of the exponential series and the inequality \(E|W|^q\le b^{q-2}EW^2\), \(q\ge2\), give, for \(|\lambda|b<3\),
\[
 E e^{\lambda W}
 \le \exp\!\left\{\frac{\lambda^2EW^2}{2(1-|\lambda|b/3)}\right\}.
\]
Applying the exponential Markov inequality to this bound cell by cell for the score and for products of locally supported regressors, then taking a union bound over \(O(J)\) nonzero spline pairs, gives
\[
 |\widehat\alpha_{1,-k}-3/2|
 =O_P\!\left(J^{5/4}\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}+J^{-s}\right),
 \qquad
 |\widehat\alpha_{0,-k}|
 =O_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{J\log n}{n}}+J^{-s}\right),
\tag{F7}
\]
and the local normal equations give
\[
 \|\widehat g_{-k}-g\|_{\infty,\{X_i:i\in I_k\}}
 =O_P\!\left(J^{5/4}\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}+J^{-s}\right).
\tag{F8}
\]
Here the approximation term follows from the degree condition and the \(C^s\) spline approximation bound; the empirical Hessian is invertible on the score neighborhood because, by (F3)--(F6), its relative deviation is
\[
 O_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{J^{5/2}(\log n)^3}{n}}\right)=o_P(1).
\tag{F9}
\]
The ridge is \(O(e^{-J})\) and hence is absorbed by the displayed orders.

Combining (F6)--(F8) over the fixed number of folds gives
\[
 \max_{1\le i\le n}|\widehat\eta_{-k(i)}(X_i)-\eta(X_i)|
 =O_P\!\left(
 J^{5/4}\frac{(\log n)^{3/2}}{\sqrt n}+J^{-s}\log n\right)=o_P(1)
\tag{F10}
\]
under the two proposed schedule conditions.  Since \(\Lambda\) is \(1/4\)-Lipschitz and \(\widehat\pi_0=1-\widehat\pi_1\),
\[
 \max_i|\widehat\pi_{0,-k(i)}(X_i)-\pi_0(X_i)|=o_P(1).
\tag{F11}
\]

The empirical fitted-propensity distribution is therefore squeezed between two translates of the empirical distribution of \(\pi_0(X)\).  The iid empirical distribution converges at every continuity point, so (F1) and monotonicity of the generalized inverse imply \(\widehat h_{0,n}\to_P2\).  Its ceiling is tight.  Every fixed lower order statistic of \(\pi_0(X_i)\) tends to \(1/2\), and (F11) hence gives
\[
 \widehat p_{0,(\lceil\widehat h_{0,n}\rceil)}\to_P\frac12,
 \qquad
 \widehat b_{0,n}\to_P\frac{\vartheta_0}{2}<\frac12.
\tag{F12}
\]
Because \(k_n/n\to0\), (F11) also makes the upper \(k_n+1\) order statistics of \(1/\widehat\pi_0\) uniformly equal to \(2+o_P(1)\).  Their Hill log-spacing average tends to zero, so the declared reciprocal convention gives \(\widehat\gamma_0\to_P\infty\).  Thus the control arm is classified as Gaussian and its drift correction is zero with probability tending to one.  Finally, (F11)--(F12) imply
\[
 \min_i\widehat\pi_{0,-k(i)}(X_i)>\widehat b_{0,n}
\]
with probability tending to one.  Every clipped weight then equals its untrimmed fitted weight, which proves all conclusions of the narrowed proposition.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose that \(\pi _0(x)+\pi _1(x)=1\), that both propensities are positive, and that, with \(\alpha_a=0\) on a bounded-support arm,
\[
 \pi_a(x)=d_a(x)^{\alpha_a}e^{g_a(x)},\qquad a\in\{0,1\},
\]
at every point at which \(d_0(x)d_1(x)>0\).  Then
\[
 \log\frac{\pi_1(x)}{\pi_0(x)}
 =\alpha_1\log d_1(x)-\alpha_0\log d_0(x)+g_1(x)-g_0(x),
\]
and consequently \(\pi_1(x)=\Lambda\{\eta(x)\}\) and \(\pi_0(x)=\Lambda\{-\eta(x)\}\).  In particular, replacing the paired boundary links by this joint log-odds representation does not remove any law satisfying the paired links.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Positivity makes both logarithms finite away from the two endpoints.  Taking logarithms of the two displayed paired links and subtracting gives
\[
 \log\pi_1(x)-\log\pi_0(x)
 =\alpha_1\log d_1(x)-\alpha_0\log d_0(x)+g_1(x)-g_0(x).
\]
The left side is \(\eta(x)\) by definition.  Since \(\pi_0=1-\pi_1\), exponentiating gives \(\pi_1/(1-\pi_1)=e^\eta\), whence
\[
 \pi_1=\frac{e^\eta}{1+e^\eta}=\Lambda(\eta),
 \qquad
 \pi_0=\frac1{1+e^\eta}=\Lambda(-\eta).
\]
All equalities hold \(P_X\)-almost surely; the endpoint values are irrelevant under the uniform chart because the endpoints are \(P_X\)-null.  Thus every law obeying the former paired links obeys the proposed joint link, which proves the claimed non-narrowing implication.

added_lemmas.statement: For every law \(P\), sample size \(N\), and finite quantile set \(\mathcal T\), the oracle statistic \(\mathsf S_{P,N}\) in \(\text{def:oracle-leading-statistic}\) is a measurable function of \((O_1,\ldots,O_N)\) invariant under every permutation of the \(N\) observations.
added_lemmas.proof_tex: For a heavy arm, every coordinate of \(\mathsf S_{a,P,N}\) is a deterministic population constant times a sum of the same measurable function of each \(O_i\), minus the corresponding deterministic expectation.  For a Gaussian arm it is a deterministic multiple of \(\sum_{i=1}^N\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O_i;\tau)\).  Finite sums of measurable functions are measurable, and reindexing either sum by a permutation leaves it unchanged.  Concatenating the two arm vectors preserves both properties.  Hence \(\mathsf S_{P,N}\) is measurable and permutation symmetric.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
On the mixed center in \(\text{prop:smooth-inclusion}\), use the joint logistic-series learner in \(\text{def:boundary-learner}\) with a quasi-uniform spline basis, \(J_n\to\infty\),
\[
 \frac{J_n^{5/2}(\log n)^3}{n}\to0,
 \qquad
 J_n^{-s}\log n\to0.
\]
Then
\[
 \inf_x\pi_0(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad t_{0,n}\to\frac12,
 \qquad h_{0,n}\to2,
\]
\[
 \widehat p_{0,(\lceil\widehat h_{0,n}\rceil)}\to_P\frac12,
 \qquad
 \widehat b_{0,n}\to_P\frac{\vartheta_0}{2}<\frac12.
\]
Consequently clipping is asymptotically inactive on the control arm, \(\widehat\gamma_0\to_P\infty\), its drift correction is zero with probability tending to one, and its feasible objective equals the untrimmed fitted-weight objective with probability tending to one.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: After replacing the separate arm fits by one joint logit fit, sample-point control of the profiled treated-endpoint log direction requires the explicit mixed-witness condition \(J_n^{5/2}(\log n)^3/n\to0\). The old condition \(J_n\log n/n\to0\) alone does not control that direction. This narrows only the estimator schedule on the same mixed law and leaves the model class and conclusion unchanged.

proposed.condition:
With \(\alpha_a=(\gamma_a-1)^{-1}\) for \(\gamma_a<\infty\) and \(\alpha_a=0\) for \(\gamma_a=\infty\), the binary propensity satisfies, \(P_X\)-almost surely on \(\{x:d_0(x)d_1(x)>0\}\),
\[
 \eta(x)=\log\frac{\pi_1(x)}{\pi_0(x)}
 =\alpha_1\log d_1(x)-\alpha_0\log d_0(x)+g_1(x)-g_0(x),
 \qquad
 (\pi_1(x),\pi_0(x))=(\Lambda\{\eta(x)\},\Lambda\{-\eta(x)\}).
\]
At a \(P_X\)-null chart endpoint, the propensity pair is assigned any coherent value in \([0,1]^2\) summing to one.

novel.justification: This is the binary-coherent joint-logit form implied by the former paired multiplicative boundary links; it permits one finite Bernoulli information geometry at both endpoints.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The old separate arm formulas imply the displayed joint log odds by subtraction, while a single logit representation prevents incoherent armwise likelihood fits. The proved helper records that this replacement does not narrow the former class.

proposed.name: Endpoint-safe joint cross-fitted logistic-series learner
proposed.construction:
Put \(L_{a,J}(x)=\log\{d_a(x)\vee e^{-J}\}\).  For each fold \(k\), define
\[
 \eta_J(x;\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\beta)
 =\alpha_1L_{1,J}(x)-\alpha_0L_{0,J}(x)
   +\sum_{j=1}^J\beta_jB_{j,J}(x),
 \qquad p_J(x;\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\beta)=\Lambda\{\eta_J(x;\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\beta)\}.
\]
Let \(\Theta_J\) be the closed convex set of \((\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\beta)\in[0,J]^2\times[-J,J]^J\) for which
\[
 e^{-J}\le p_J(x;\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\beta)\le1-e^{-J}
 \quad\text{for every }x\in[0,1].
\]
The fitted parameter \((\widehat\alpha_{0,-k},\widehat\alpha_{1,-k},\widehat\beta_{-k})\) is the unique maximizer over \(\Theta_{J_n}\) of
\[
 \sum_{i\notin I_k}\left[A_i\log p_{J_n}(X_i;\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\beta)
 +(1-A_i)\log\{1-p_{J_n}(X_i;\alpha_0,\alpha_1,\beta)\}\right]
 -e^{-J_n}\left(\alpha_0^2+\alpha_1^2+\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}\beta_j^2\right).
\]
Strict concavity of the ridge makes the maximizer unique.  Set
\[
 \widehat\eta_{-k}(x)=\eta_{J_n}(x;\widehat\alpha_{0,-k},\widehat\alpha_{1,-k},\widehat\beta_{-k}),
 \qquad
 \widehat\pi_{1,-k}(x)=\Lambda\{\widehat\eta_{-k}(x)\},
 \qquad
 \widehat\pi_{0,-k}(x)=1-\widehat\pi_{1,-k}(x).
\]
Thus every fitted pair is binary coherent and the clipped log coordinates make its endpoint values finite.
inputs: the prespecified two endpoint charts and spline dictionary
the deterministic compact probability-range and ridge rules

proposed_core_edits.reason: One constrained Bernoulli likelihood gives score \((A-\pi_1)v\), information \(E_P(\pi_0\pi_1v^2)\), and fitted probabilities that sum to one pointwise.

proposed.name: Binary-coherent tail-band escape perturbation
proposed.construction:
Fix a target arm \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\) and put \(\epsilon_{a,n}=M_n^{-(\gamma_a-1)}\).  On the fitted tail band \(\{x:\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)\le M_n/\widehat h_{a,n}\}\), set
\[
 \widehat\pi^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,-k}(x)
 =\min\{1-e^{-J_n},(1+\epsilon_{a,n})\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)\},
 \qquad
 \widehat\pi^{\mathrm{esc}}_{1-a,-k}(x)=1-\widehat\pi^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,-k}(x).
\]
Outside that band leave the fitted pair unchanged.  If the lower range constraint is reached after complementation, project the target probability onto \([e^{-J_n},1-e^{-J_n}]\) and again define the other probability as its complement.  Compute \(E^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,n}\) and \(D^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,n}\) from this target-arm perturbation.  The construction perturbs one tail probability while preserving \(\widehat\pi^{\mathrm{esc}}_{0,-k}+\widehat\pi^{\mathrm{esc}}_{1,-k}=1\) pointwise.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Perturbing one fitted arm without changing its complement violates binary coherence. The replacement preserves the target perturbation and defines the other arm as its complement.

proposed.name: Refitted arm-vector \(m\)-out-of-\(n\) procedure and raw scalar diagnostic
proposed.construction:
Choose \(m\to\infty\) with \(m/n\to0\).  Conditionally on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), draw \(B\) uniformly from the subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) of size \(m\).  For each realized \(B\), refit the joint learner, generalized-inverse scales, clips, preliminary quantiles, endpoint corrections, and densities using only observations indexed by \(B\).  Define
\[
 V_{B,a}(\tau)=\frac m{\widehat H_{a,m,B}}
 \{\widehat q_{a,B}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)\},
 \qquad
 T_{B,n}(\tau)=\widehat\ell_{1,n}V_{B,1}(\tau)-\widehat\ell_{0,n}V_{B,0}(\tau).
\]
The conditional coordinate quantiles \(c_{n,p}(\tau)\), maximum \(M_{B,n}\), maximum quantile \(c^{\max}_{n,p}\), and band \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{sim}}\) are then exactly as displayed in the frozen construction.  For comparison only, define the raw scalar refit by
\[
 T^{\mathrm{raw}}_{B,n}(\tau)
 =\frac m{\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\widehat H_{a,m,B}}
 \left[
 \{\widehat q_{1,B}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\widehat q_{0,B}^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)\}
 -\{\widehat q_1^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\widehat q_0^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)\}
 \right].
\]
This raw statistic is an internal diagnostic and is not attributed to a published procedure.
inputs: a conditional uniform randomizer over size-\(m\) subsets, or exact enumeration

proposed_core_edits.reason: The arm-vector algorithm is retained, every subsample now refits the coherent joint learner, and the previously unnamed raw scalar comparison is defined only as an internal diagnostic.

proposed.statement:

\[
 \frac{J_n^{5/2}(\log n)^3}{n}\to0,

\]
Then
\[
 \inf_x\pi_0(x)=\frac12,
 \qquad t_{0,n}\to\frac12,

\]
\[

Consequently clipping is asymptotically inactive on the control arm, \(\widehat\gamma_0\to_P\infty\), its drift correction is zero with probability tending to one, and its feasible objective equals the untrimmed fitted-weight objective with probability tending to one.
proposed.justification: On the explicit mixed chart, the two profiled endpoint directions can be bounded directly; the resulting sample-point consistency proves fixed-rank clipping, bounded-arm Hill classification, and disappearance of the control correction.
proposed.gap: This is a centering and implementation sanity result on the explicit mixed witness, not a uniform first-stage theorem on the whole smooth class.
proposed.consumer: It verifies that the coherent joint fit does not spuriously clip or drift-correct the bounded control arm on the mixed witness.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A uniform lower bound and empirical concentration theorem for the joint design formed by the two clipped log coordinates and the quasi-uniform spline basis, after profiling both log directions, on every law in the frozen smooth class.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen assumptions control the marginal Hall tails of the propensities but impose no regularity tying the measurable chart maps \(d_a\) to the spatial quasi-uniform spline cells. They therefore do not exclude near-collinearity of a log-chart direction with the spline space or guarantee the asserted cellwise rank uniformly. The score and information are finite after the joint-logit repair, but the required uniform eigenvalue and Hessian bounds do not follow from the stated primitives.
open_obligations.attempted: Differentiated the coherent likelihood, localized its weight at both endpoints, rescaled the boundary cells, and profiled the two log directions. The calculation closes for the explicit charts \(d_1(x)=x\) and \(d_0(x)=1-x\), but the step from Hall marginal tails to a uniform spatial cell bound fails for the general measurable chart maps allowed by the class.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For every joint-logit direction \(v\), direct differentiation gives
\[
 \dot\ell_\eta(v)=(A-\pi_1)v,
 \qquad
 -E_P\ddot\ell_\eta(v,w)=E_P\{\pi_0\pi_1vw\}.
\]
Thus the repaired likelihood has finite information and the correct two-endpoint weight.  Near arm \(a\)'s endpoint, opposite overlap makes \(\pi_0\pi_1\asymp\pi_a\).  On the explicit charts \(d_1=x\), \(d_0=1-x\), the first and last cell calculations give profiled log-direction norms of orders \(J^{-(\alpha_1+1)}\) and \(J^{-(\alpha_0+1)}\), respectively, so the candidate global eigenvalue is \(J^{-(\alpha_\star+1)}\).  What is not established uniformly on the frozen class is that these cellwise bounds survive arbitrary admissible chart maps and simultaneous profiling against the quasi-uniform spline space.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Uniform samplewise approximation of the feasible compensated heavy-arm quantile by the newly defined centered population-clipped oracle statistic.
open_obligations.obstruction: The score-transfer bound \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\) and the interior discrepancy bound both depend on the unresolved uniform joint-sieve information theorem.
open_obligations.attempted: Rechecked Hall inversion, point-process compensation, clipping drift, Knight curvature, and the empirical correction algebra; these oracle-side steps close, but they cannot turn into a feasible theorem without the first-stage transfer bound.
open_obligations.partial_result: With the true propensity and population clip, Hall inversion, the endpoint mark condition, and the exact Knight identity yield the centered Lévy score \(\mathsf Z_{a,\theta}\), clipping mean \(\mu_{a,\theta}(\tau)=-\theta_a^{\gamma_a-1}m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}/\gamma_a\), and curvature \(f_a(\tau)t^2/2\).  The proposed statistic \(\mathsf S_{a,P,N}\) is the centered oracle score divided by \(f_a\).  Feasible samplewise approximation remains conditional on the unresolved uniform joint-sieve transfer bound.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The unconditional necessity theorem for the binary-coherent escape learner.
open_obligations.obstruction: The compensator shift survives the coherent complement perturbation, but the claims for \(E^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,n}\) and \(D^{\mathrm{esc}}_{a,n}\) require the base learner rates left open at the boundary-likelihood node.
open_obligations.attempted: Perturbed the target tail probability, recomputed its complement, and repeated the Hall-band mean and variance calculation. The deterministic shift closes conditionally on the missing base rate.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For a target heavy arm, the binary-coherent perturbation multiplies the target tail probability by \(1+\epsilon_n\), where \(\epsilon_n=M_n^{-(\gamma_a-1)}\), and changes its complement accordingly.  Conditional on the base learner satisfying \(E_{a,n}=o_P(\epsilon_n)\), the Hall compensator over \(C/h_{a,n}<\pi_a<M_n/h_{a,n}\) is
\[
 -\epsilon_n\frac n{h_{a,n}}
 \int_{C/h_{a,n}}^{M_n/h_{a,n}}\kappa_{a,\tau}(t)\,dF_a^\pi(t)
 \longrightarrow-m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}.
\]
The complement perturbation is negligible at the target endpoint by opposite overlap.  Hence the old shift calculation survives algebraically, but its unconditional premise is the unresolved boundary-likelihood rate.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The uniform learned-propensity influence-function expansion under the joint logistic series fit.
open_obligations.obstruction: Although the exact cross-fit evaluation variance and its regular-chart cell orders are now exposed, the frozen general chart assumptions do not supply the uniform projection and empirical-Hessian bounds needed to make those orders valid throughout the class.
open_obligations.attempted: Recomputed the joint-logit Riesz representers, verified the AIPW algebra and shared cross-arm covariance, and derived the three boundary-cell candidates \(J/n\), \(J\log J/n\), and \(J^{2\alpha_a}/n\). The missing spatial cell-rank theorem prevents a uniform remainder conclusion.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditional on a training fold, the exact evaluation variance is
\[
 E_P\!\left[\pi_a(X)left\{\frac1{\widehat\pi_a(X)}-\frac1{\pi_a(X)}\right\}^2\right]
 =E_P\!\left[\frac{\{\widehat\pi_a(X)-\pi_a(X)\}^2}
 {\pi_a(X)\widehat\pi_a(X)^2}\right].
\]
Under relative-error localization and the regular chart cell calculation, its stochastic part has the candidate order
\[
 \frac1n\begin{cases}
 J,&\alpha_a<1/2,\\
 J\log J,&\alpha_a=1/2,\\
 J^{2\alpha_a},&\alpha_a>1/2,
 \end{cases}
\]
plus the approximation contribution \(O(J^{-2s})\).  For the joint logit information \(E_P(\pi_0\pi_1vw)\), the two signed-functional Riesz representers are \(r_{1,\tau}=m_{1,\tau}/\pi_1\) and \(r_{0,\tau}=-m_{0,\tau}/\pi_0\).  In either arm,
\[
 \frac{\mathbf1\{A=a\}\psi_{a,\tau}(Y)}{\pi_a(X)}
 -(A-\pi_1(X))r_{a,\tau}(X)
 =m_{a,\tau}(X)+\frac{\mathbf1\{A=a\}\{\psi_{a,\tau}(Y)-m_{a,\tau}(X)\}}{\pi_a(X)},
\]
with the evident sign already incorporated in \(r_{0,\tau}\).  Division by \(f_a(\tau)\) gives the declared influence function and its cross-arm covariance.  Uniform projection and empirical-Hessian control on the frozen chart class remain unresolved.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Uniform bounded-Lipschitz approximation of the normalized feasible QTE to the moving row law.
open_obligations.obstruction: The deterministic arm recombination is valid, but at least one required samplewise arm approximation is unproved because both the heavy and learned Gaussian branches depend on the unresolved joint-sieve step.
open_obligations.attempted: Verified the exact scale identity and Lipschitz recombination, including equal and unequal arm scales. No independent route bypasses the armwise first-stage expansion.
open_obligations.partial_result:
If each feasible arm statistic is samplewise \(o_P(1)\) from \(\mathsf S_{a,P,n}\) and the oracle vector law is uniformly close to \(L_P\), then the exact identity
\[
 \frac n{H_{P,n}}(\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}-\Delta_P)
 =\ell_{1,P,n}\frac n{H_{1,P,n}}(\widehat q_1^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_{1,P})
 -\ell_{0,P,n}\frac n{H_{0,P,n}}(\widehat q_0^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_{0,P})
\]
and the fact that the recombination map has Lipschitz norm at most two yield bounded-Lipschitz approximation to \(Z_{P,n}\).  This deterministic recombination is proved, but its armwise stochastic premises remain open.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Uniform conditional approximation and pointwise or maximum-band coverage for the refitted arm-vector statistic.
open_obligations.obstruction: The oracle leading statistic is now explicit and symmetric, but the complete-subsample argument requires uniform samplewise \(o_P(1)\) approximation of every feasible full and refitted arm vector to that statistic. This is not supplied by distributional convergence and remains blocked by the joint-sieve expansion.
open_obligations.attempted: Defined the symmetric oracle statistic, proved its permutation symmetry, retained the Hoeffding complete-subsample variance calculation, and defined the raw scalar comparator internally. The missing feasible-to-oracle coupling prevents the coverage step.
open_obligations.partial_result: The oracle statistic \(\mathsf S_{P,N}\) is now explicitly defined and proved permutation symmetric.  For every bounded one-Lipschitz \(g\), the complete size-\(m\) subsample average of \(g(\mathsf S_{P,m})\) has variance at most \(4m/n\) by its Hoeffding decomposition.  Thus the complete-subsample step is valid once one proves uniformly that each feasible refit is samplewise \(o_P(1)\) from \(\mathsf S_{P,m}\).  That approximation is precisely what the unresolved joint-sieve expansion must supply.  The newly defined \(T^{\mathrm{raw}}_{B,n}\) is only an internal diagnostic, not a negative claim about a published method.

prose_updates.tldr: The binary propensity model and learner are repaired as one endpoint-safe joint logistic series fit, whose score is \((A-\pi_1)v\) and whose information is \(E_P(\pi_0\pi_1vw)\). The mixed and two-heavy examples remain in the model, and bounded-control clipping and classification are proved on the mixed chart under the corrected joint-fit schedule. The frozen class, however, does not regularize the chart maps enough to prove the uniform profiled spline-rank and empirical-Hessian bound. Consequently the advertised heavy transfer, learned Gaussian branch, moving QTE law, and refitted coverage remain explicit downstream obligations rather than established conclusions. The oracle leading arm vector and an internal raw scalar diagnostic are now defined coherently.

project_justification.gap: Existing regular-overlap and weak-overlap references do not supply the two-endpoint joint-logit spline rank theorem needed here. More basically, the current frozen chart assumptions do not themselves imply that theorem.
project_justification.niche: The intended contribution remains feasible QTE limit and inference theory under weak overlap, but it requires a binary-coherent first stage and a samplewise oracle comparator before moving-law subsampling can be justified.
project_justification.fill: This repair establishes binary coherence, the exact likelihood score and information, preservation of the explicit model witnesses, a corrected bounded-control sanity theorem, the exact Gaussian evaluation variance, joint-logit Riesz algebra, and a permutation-symmetric oracle statistic. It does not claim the uniform feasible limit or coverage theorems until the chart-to-spline rank obstruction is resolved.

sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is binary and the two fitted probabilities are generated by one joint log odds, so they sum to one pointwise. Heavy and finite-variance labels remain population regimes separated from \(\gamma=2\) only in the intended downstream theory.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each fold now fits one constrained and ridged logistic series with clipped log coordinates for both endpoints, setting \(\widehat\pi_{0,-k}=1-\widehat\pi_{1,-k}\). On the explicit mixed chart, sample-point consistency of the bounded arm is proved under \(J_n^{5/2}(\log n)^3/n\to0\) and \(J_n^{-s}\log n\to0\). No uniform rate over the full frozen smooth class is claimed.

prose_updates.related_work: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky provide the observed-true-propensity weak-overlap quantile benchmark; Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder and Firpo provide regular estimated-propensity context. Ma and Wang and Khan and Tamer are retained only as limited-overlap and support-condition background. Knight supplies the classical check-loss decomposition, and Politis, Romano, and Wolf supply general subsampling context; neither proves the paper-specific learned-propensity coupling. Dorn is weak-overlap nuisance-tail context, and Sant'Anna, Song, and Xu is propensity-balance context. No cited result is asserted to establish the open two-endpoint spline theorem, and the raw scalar diagnostic is not attributed to any published method.
prose_updates.interpretation: The joint-logit repair removes the incoherence of separately fitted binary arms and exposes the correct boundary weight \(\pi_0\pi_1\). The remaining failure is not a variance-symbol typo: Hall marginal tails do not control how an arbitrary measurable endpoint chart aligns with quasi-uniform spline cells. Moving-law recombination and complete-subsample algebra are therefore conditional architecture, not current inference guarantees.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Uniform information, signed-Riesz rates, feasible oracle transfer, the learned Gaussian expansion, joint QTE convergence, and refitted pointwise or simultaneous coverage are unproved on the current frozen class. The precise missing ingredient is a uniform lower-rank and empirical-Hessian bound for the two profiled log-chart directions relative to the spatial spline basis. The calculation is valid for the explicit regular charts \(d_1(x)=x\) and \(d_0(x)=1-x\), but the class allows more general measurable charts. The critical fold-law question also remains separate and open.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established in this round are the joint log-odds implication of the former paired links, nonempty mixed and two-heavy witnesses, finite joint Bernoulli information, bounded-control clipping and Hill-classification sanity on the mixed chart under its corrected schedule, exact Gaussian evaluation-variance and Riesz algebra, and permutation symmetry of an explicit oracle leading statistic. The heavy, Gaussian, joint-QTE, and subsampling theorems remain open because the general chart-to-spline rank step is absent. The raw scalar construction is only an internal diagnostic; no negative claim about a published estimator or guarantee is made.
